title: Site Traffic & Mobile Plant
whatItIs: Every year workers are killed on sites by moving or overturning vehicles. Most transport accidents come from not keeping pedestrians and vehicles apart.

keyFacts.text: A site MUST be organised so pedestrians and vehicles can move safely, so far as reasonably practicable.
Traffic routes MUST be suitable, signed where needed, regularly checked and properly maintained.
You MUST NOT ride on a site vehicle except in a safe place provided for that purpose.
Steps MUST be taken to stop vehicles falling into excavations, pits or water, e.g. stop blocks.

keyFacts: Only trained drivers authorised for that vehicle should drive site plant.
Leaving a vehicle? Turn the engine off and take the key.

items.title: Separate gates and walkways
items.text: Separate ways in for vehicles and people. Firm walkways kept clear.

items.title: Crossing points
items.text: Signed and well lit, where drivers and pedestrians see each other.

items.title: One-way systems
items.text: One-way systems and turning areas cut reversing. Speed limits clearly signed.

a.label: Site layout and planning
points: Put in place first: removes the risk

b.label: Mirrors, cameras and alarms
points: Help drivers see and warn people

onTheTest.question: A pedestrian walkway has to cross a site haul road. What should be provided?
options: A clearly signed, well-lit crossing point with clear views
A sign telling drivers to use the horn
A rule that pedestrians run across quickly
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 271: where walkways cross vehicle routes, provide a clearly signed, well-lit crossing point where both can see each other.

onTheTest.question: You need to speak to the driver of a working excavator. What should you do?
options: Walk up behind it and tap the cab
Stand in front of the bucket and wave
Get the driver's attention and wait until the machine is at rest
Climb onto the tracks to be seen
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 306: make the driver aware you want to approach and make sure the machine is safely at rest first.

traps: Don't block walkways: it forces people to step into the vehicle route.
Use the pedestrian routes and site rules you were shown at induction.
Don't park on slopes: failed handbrakes cause runaway vehicles.
Don't drive any site vehicle unless you are trained and authorised for it.
